{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**Prepared by:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Subject:** Verified playbook findings on the Master Services Agreement

## Executive summary

We have completed our playbook review of the Master Services Agreement. The risk-allocation core of the document is in good shape: Vendor indemnification (§ 20), IP and Customer Data ownership (§ 14), the mutual liability cap and carve-outs (§ 21), assignment and change of control (§ 24), the licence grant (§ 13), transition assistance and data return (§ 11), governing law and venue (§ 28), and Vendor insurance (§ 18) all meet our preferred positions and require no redline.

Our concerns are concentrated in the commercial-restraint and administrative provisions, several of which are internally inconsistent with the protections Vendor has already conceded in § 12.3 (no exclusivity, no MFN, no minimum-volume, no no-hire commitment). Eight items require action: full-term sole-source exclusivity (§ 2.2, also driving the minimum-commitment finding), uncapped Customer-payable liquidated damages (§ 7.6), a Customer-side MFN (§ 7.2), a one-sided 18-month no-hire (§ 12.4), unlimited unannounced audits with remote system access (§ 22.1), a 180-day non-renewal notice window (§ 8.2), and the absence of any termination-for-convenience right against a three-year committed term (§ 9).

One finding is recorded as needs review for internal purposes only: the warranty period in § 19.2 is spelled out as "ninety days" rather than "90 days," which caused an automated check to fail. On its substance the warranty package (§§ 19.1–19.5) meets or exceeds our position, and we do not propose raising it with Vendor.

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 20.1 (with §§ 20.2–20.5, 21.3) |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 14.1 (with §§ 13.2, 14.2–14.4, 15.1) |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | Compliant | § 21.1 (with §§ 21.2–21.4, 18.2) |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1 (with §§ 24.2–24.4) |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 2.2 |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 7.6 |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13.1 (with §§ 13.2–13.3) |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 12.3 |
| High | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 12.4 |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Missing** | § 9 |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | **Deviation** | § 22.1 |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28.1 (with §§ 28.2–28.3) |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | **Deviation** | § 7.2 |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase / volume restrictions | **Deviation** | § 2.2 |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | **Deviation** | § 8.2 |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § 11.1 (with §§ 11.2–11.3) |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Needs review (internal only) | § 19.1 (period at § 19.2) |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1 (with § 18.2) |

## Walk-away items

The following provisions sit in walk-away territory under our playbook and must be resolved before signature:

1. **§ 2.2 — Sole and exclusive provider.** Full-term sole-source exclusivity for hosted analytics services, with no category or duration limit and no performance-based exit. Fails the fallback (category-specific, 12 months, exit on service-level or delivery failure) and contradicts §§ 2.1 and 12.3. It also commits 100% of our demand, which is why it is separately flagged as a volume restriction. *Position:* Vendor is a non-exclusive provider; we remain free to source from third parties and pay only for Services ordered.
2. **§ 7.6 — Customer-payable liquidated damages.** USD 25,000 per day for any delay in providing a dependency: one-way, uncapped, no materiality threshold and no grace or notice mechanic, and not evidently capped by §§ 21.2–21.3. *Position:* replace the payment with day-for-day schedule relief for Vendor.
3. **§ 12.4 — 18-month no-hire.** One-sided, covers any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term, bars "engage" as well as solicit, and has no general-advertising carve-out; it also conflicts with § 12.3. *Position:* mutual, personnel directly involved in the Services only, 12 months from the end of their involvement, no no-hire, customary carve-outs (fallback).
4. **§ 22.1 — Unlimited unannounced audits with remote system access.** Fails the fallback on frequency, notice and system access, and conflicts with the acceptable §§ 22.2–22.3. *Position:* once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, independent auditor under confidentiality, off-site where practicable, no remote or direct system access.
5. **§ 7.2 — Customer-side MFN.** Open-ended obligation to extend Vendor the best terms we give any other technology supplier, with no product limit, no 12-month cap and no comparison carve-outs; contradicts § 12.3. *Position:* delete (no Vendor-granted MFN exists to preserve).
6. **§ 9 — No termination for convenience.** Section 9 offers only for-cause exits, while § 8.1 commits us to a three-year term. *Position:* insert a 30-day convenience right with pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, confirming Vendor has none.

## Next steps

1. **Issue the redlines** on §§ 2.2, 7.2, 7.6, 8.2, 9 (new 9.4), 12.4 and 22.1, each with a short `[Playbook]` rationale and the fallback offered where sensible (§ 12.4 no-hire; § 22.1 audit mechanics).
2. **Lead the negotiation with the internal-consistency point.** Sections 2.2, 7.2 and 12.4 each contradict § 12.3, in which Vendor already acknowledges that we have made no exclusivity, MFN, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment; conforming those clauses to § 12.3 should be presented as clean-up rather than a new ask.
3. **Renewal window (§ 8.2).** Seek 30 days' non-renewal notice plus a Vendor renewal reminder in a single edit. Renewal pricing needs no change — § 8.3 already caps uplift at the lesser of CPI and 3%.
4. **Confirm the § 7.6 liability interaction.** If the clause survives in any form, ensure the resulting exposure is expressly subject to the § 21.1 cap and not treated as an Excluded Claim.
5. **Warranty housekeeping (internal).** Optionally render § 19.2 as "ninety (90) days" for mechanical clarity. This is non-substantive; we do not intend to raise it as a negotiation item.
6. **Leave the compliant provisions untouched**, in particular § 12.3, §§ 20–21, § 14 and § 24, which are favourable to us; reopening them invites erosion.
7. **Escalate for business sign-off** on the two items with the greatest commercial content: exclusivity and volume freedom (§ 2.2) and the convenience-termination right against the three-year term (§§ 8.1, 9)."}
